question: Can one attain final liberation even when dying without memory in any place?
premises: Death may occur in a holy place or an impure place.
Memory may be lost at the time of death.
Liberation can be simultaneous with knowledge.
inference: Therefore one who is liberated simultaneously with knowledge attains sorrowless final liberation regardless of place or memory.
uncertainties: jñānasamakālamuktaḥ may refer to liberation at the same moment as knowledge arises or is fully manifest.
plain_english: Whether at a holy place or in the house of an outcaste, even if memory is lost, one who abandons the body liberated simultaneously with knowledge goes to final liberation, free from sorrow.
